## Introduction

Practice the geometry operations from today's lecture using Swiss spatial data. Choose at least 2 scenarios.

:::{.callout-note title="No AI!"}
These tasks were specifically designed to be solvable without AI. Solve them without it!
:::

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Data is available on Moodle, under *Spatial Analysis I*:

- **swissBOUNDARIES3D.gpkg**: Canton of Luzern boundary
- **swiss_TLM3D.gpkg**:
  - `tlm_bb` — land cover polygons with attribute `objektart` (Wald, Feuchtgebiet, Stehende Gewaesser, etc.)

All data use CRS EPSG:2056 (CH1903+ / LV95).


## Scenario 1: Centroids and Point Placement

Analyse land cover polygons in Canton Luzern to understand when centroids misbehave.

- **1.1:** Load all wetland polygons ("Feuchtgebiet") within Canton Luzern. Compute their centroids using `st_centroid()`. How many wetland polygons are there?
- **1.2:** Use `st_within()` to check whether each centroid lies inside its source polygon. What proportion of centroids fall **outside**?
- **1.3:** For the first five wetlands whose centroid is outside, compute `st_point_on_surface()` as well. Map these polygons with both point types (centroid in red, point-on-surface in blue). What do you notice about the polygon shapes?


```{r}
luzern <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_II/swissBOUNDARIES3D.gpkg")
tlm_bb <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_II/swiss_TLM3D.gpkg", "tlm_bb")
tlm_bb <- st_set_crs(tlm_bb, 2056)

# 1.1: Load wetland polygons within Luzern
wetlands <- tlm_bb |>
  filter(objektart == "Feuchtgebiet") |>
  st_filter(luzern) |>
  st_intersection(luzern)

nrow(wetlands)

# 1.2: Check which centroids fall outside their polygon
centroids <- st_centroid(wetlands)
inside    <- st_within(centroids, wetlands, sparse = FALSE) |> diag()
sum(!inside)
mean(!inside) * 100   # percentage outside

# 1.3: Visualise first 5 problematic cases
problematic   <- wetlands[!inside, ] |> head(5)
prob_centroid <- st_centroid(problematic)
prob_pos      <- st_point_on_surface(problematic)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = problematic,   fill = "gray90", color = "gray50") +
  geom_sf(data = prob_centroid, color = "firebrick", size = 3) +
  geom_sf(data = prob_pos,      color = "steelblue",  size = 3, shape = 17) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title    = "Centroids vs. Point on Surface",
    subtitle = "Red circle: st_centroid()   Blue triangle: st_point_on_surface()"
  )
```


## Scenario 2: Affine Transformations

Apply shift, scale, and rotation to the Canton Luzern boundary.

- **2.1:** Load the canton geometry. Drop Z coordinates with `st_zm()` and compute its centroid.
- **2.2:** Create three transformed versions of the geometry:
  - Shifted 20 km to the east
  - Scaled to 50% of its original size around the centroid
  - Rotated 45° around the centroid (you will need to write a `rotation()` function)
- **2.3:** Map all four versions (original + three transformations) side by side.
- **2.4** *(Challenge)*: Compose two operations — shift 10 km east, then rotate 20° around the new centroid. Compare this with rotating first and then shifting. Are the results the same?


```{r}
luzern     <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_II/swissBOUNDARIES3D.gpkg")
luzern_sfc <- st_zm(st_geometry(luzern))
center     <- st_centroid(luzern_sfc)

# 2.2: Three transformations
luzern_shifted <- luzern_sfc + c(20000, 0)
st_crs(luzern_shifted) <- st_crs(luzern)

luzern_scaled <- (luzern_sfc - center) * 0.5 + center
st_crs(luzern_scaled) <- st_crs(luzern)

rotation <- function(deg) {
  r <- deg * pi / 180
  matrix(c(cos(r), -sin(r), sin(r), cos(r)), nrow = 2, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
}

luzern_rotated <- (luzern_sfc - center) * rotation(45) + center
st_crs(luzern_rotated) <- st_crs(luzern)

# 2.3: Side-by-side plot
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = luzern_sfc,     fill = "gray80") + theme_void() + labs(title = "Original")
p2 <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = luzern_shifted, fill = "gray80") + theme_void() + labs(title = "Shift +20 km east")
p3 <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = luzern_scaled,  fill = "gray80") + theme_void() + labs(title = "Scale × 0.5")
p4 <- ggplot() + geom_sf(data = luzern_rotated, fill = "gray80") + theme_void() + labs(title = "Rotate 45°")

(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4)

# 2.4: Order matters — shift then rotate vs. rotate then shift
luzern_shift_rot <- luzern_sfc + c(10000, 0)
center_shifted   <- st_centroid(luzern_shift_rot)
luzern_shift_rot <- (luzern_shift_rot - center_shifted) * rotation(20) + center_shifted
st_crs(luzern_shift_rot) <- st_crs(luzern)

luzern_rot_shift <- (luzern_sfc - center) * rotation(20) + center + c(10000, 0)
st_crs(luzern_rot_shift) <- st_crs(luzern)

pa <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = luzern_sfc,      fill = "gray80", color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sf(data = luzern_shift_rot, fill = NA, color = "steelblue") +
  theme_void() + labs(title = "Shift, then rotate")

pb <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = luzern_sfc,      fill = "gray80", color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sf(data = luzern_rot_shift, fill = NA, color = "firebrick") +
  theme_void() + labs(title = "Rotate, then shift")

pa + pb
```


## Scenario 3: Simplification

Compare how `st_simplify()` and `ms_simplify()` behave, and discover the topology problem.

- **3.1:** Load forest polygons ("Wald") within Canton Luzern. Apply `st_simplify()` with tolerances of 100 m and 1 000 m. How many vertices does each version have compared to the original?
- **3.2:** Load five neighbouring European countries (Switzerland, Germany, France, Austria, Italy) using `rnaturalearth::ne_countries()`, transform to EPSG:3857. Apply `st_simplify()` with a tolerance of 50 000 m. Do gaps appear between countries?
- **3.3:** Apply `rmapshaper::ms_simplify()` with `keep = 0.1` to the same dataset. How do the shared borders compare?
- **3.4:** Map all three versions (original, `st_simplify`, `ms_simplify`) side by side.


```{r}
luzern <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_II/swissBOUNDARIES3D.gpkg")
tlm_bb <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_II/swiss_TLM3D.gpkg", "tlm_bb")
tlm_bb <- st_set_crs(tlm_bb, 2056)

# 3.1: Vertex counts at different tolerances
forests <- tlm_bb |>
  filter(objektart == "Wald") |>
  st_filter(luzern)

n0     <- nrow(st_coordinates(forests))
f_100  <- st_simplify(forests, dTolerance = 100,  preserveTopology = TRUE)
f_1000 <- st_simplify(forests, dTolerance = 1000, preserveTopology = TRUE)
n1     <- nrow(st_coordinates(f_100))
n2     <- nrow(st_coordinates(f_1000))

cat("Original:", n0, "vertices\n")
cat("100 m tolerance:", n1, "vertices\n")
cat("1 000 m tolerance:", n2, "vertices\n")

# 3.2 & 3.3: Shared-border comparison
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rmapshaper)

neighbors <- ne_countries(continent = "Europe", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(name %in% c("Switzerland", "Germany", "France", "Austria", "Italy")) |>
  st_transform(3857) |>
  select(name) |>
  st_cast("POLYGON")

neighbors <- neighbors |>
  mutate(area = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  slice_max(area, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

n_simp <- st_simplify(neighbors, dTolerance = 50000)
n_ms   <- ms_simplify(neighbors, keep = 0.1)

# 3.4: Side-by-side
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(neighbors) + geom_sf(aes(fill = name), show.legend = FALSE) + theme_void() + labs(title = "Original")
p2 <- ggplot(n_simp)    + geom_sf(aes(fill = name), show.legend = FALSE) + theme_void() + labs(title = "st_simplify", subtitle = "gaps visible")
p3 <- ggplot(n_ms)      + geom_sf(aes(fill = name), show.legend = FALSE) + theme_void() + labs(title = "ms_simplify", subtitle = "topology preserved")

p1 + p2 + p3
```
